tool.name: roast
tool.description: : reference-guided multiple alignment of pairwise MAFs (multiz autoMZ)
tool.command: ## Galaxy flattens newlines in <command>, so the work is a POSIX sh script (the multiz image is BusyBox). ## Its inputs are argv, never Cheetah, so the same script runs as a UDT. sh '$script' '$reference' '$tree' '$output' '$pairwise' ## ⚠ The script uses backticks, never \$( ): in a UDT, \$( ... ) is Galaxy's expression syntax, and a ## shell command substitution written that way is evaluated as JavaScript and fails the job.

configfiles.configfile: set -eu ref="\$1"; treefile="\$2"; output="\$3"; files="\$4" \#\# No input at all can only mean the inputs did not arrive (a piece of a split always has at least one \#\# species); roast would run on stubs alone and write headers with no blocks, so refuse instead. [ -n "\$files" ] || { echo "no pairwise MAFs reached the job" >&2; exit 1; } case "\$ref" in ''|*[!A-Za-z0-9_]*) echo "reference name must be letters, digits or _: \$ref" >&2; exit 1;; esac mkdir work \#\# UCSC's tree preparation (kent src/hg/makeDb/doc/hg38/multiz5way.txt): branch lengths, the ';' and \#\# newlines go, commas become spaces: ((hg38 (tupChi1 galVar1)) (mm10 cavPor3)). tree=`sed 's/:[-0-9.eE]*//g; s/;//; /^ *\$/d' "\$treefile" | tr '\n' ' ' | sed 's/ //g; s/,/ /g'` leaves=" `echo "\$tree" | tr '()' ' ' | tr -s ' '` " case "\$leaves" in *" \$ref "*) ;; *) echo "reference \$ref is not in the tree" >&2; exit 1;; esac \#\# The species is read from the file, not from a dataset name: the first row that is not the reference. \#\# A file with no blocks names no species and is skipped; the stub below covers that species. IFS=',' for f in \$files; do unset IFS name=`awk -v ref="\$ref" '/^s /{ split(\$2, p, "."); if (p[1] != ref) { print p[1]; exit } }' "\$f"` IFS=',' [ -n "\$name" ] || continue case "\$leaves" in *" \$name "*) ;; *) echo "\$name is not in the tree" >&2; exit 1;; esac if [ -e "work/\$ref.\$name.sing.maf" ]; then echo "\$name is given twice" >&2; exit 1; fi ln -s "\$f" "work/\$ref.\$name.sing.maf" done unset IFS \#\# a species in the tree with no alignment in this piece gets UCSC's empty stub (autoMultiz.csh) for s in \$leaves; do [ "\$s" = "\$ref" ] && continue [ -e "work/\$ref.\$s.sing.maf" ] || echo '\#\#maf version=1 scoring=autoMZ' > "work/\$ref.\$s.sing.maf" done echo "tree: \$tree" cd work mkdir tmp roast + T="\$PWD/tmp" E="\$ref" "\$tree" \$ref.*.sing.maf out.maf > /dev/null cd .. mv work/out.maf "\$output"

param.name: pairwise
param.label: Pairwise MAFs, one per species
param.help: One MAF per species, its rows named species.sequence (mm10.chr1), the reference as the top row of every block, sorted by reference position. The species is read from the rows, so the dataset names do not matter; map over the outer level of a nested list to run one piece per inner list.

param.name: reference
param.label: Reference name
param.help: As it prefixes the reference rows (hg38 for hg38.chr1). Letters, digits and _ only.

param.name: tree
param.label: Species tree
param.help: Newick; branch lengths are ignored. Every species (and the reference) must be a leaf.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Runs ``roast`` (multiz's ``autoMZ``) over one set of pairwise MAFs that share a reference, as UCSC's ``autoMultiz.csh`` does for each piece of a multizNway build:
::
autoMZ + T=$tmp E=$db "`cat tree.nh`" $db.*.sing.maf $c
Each input becomes ``<reference>.<species>.sing.maf``, the species read from the file's first non-reference row, so dataset names play no part. A species in the tree with no input, or an empty one, gets UCSC's stub ``##maf version=1 scoring=autoMZ``, so one piece of a genome split can be run without every species aligning to it.
The tree is prepared as UCSC does: branch lengths, ``;`` and newlines are removed and commas become spaces, giving ``((hg38 (tupChi1 galVar1)) (mm10 cavPor3))``. UCSC's scripts also strip a lowercase ``name_`` prefix, which exists for their common-name trees; it is not applied here, because the leaves must be the species names the MAF rows use.
.. warning:: Pairwise inputs must be sorted by reference position. multiz merges unsorted input wrongly with exit status 0. ``netToAxt | axtSort | axtToMaf`` (or ``mafSplit`` of such a file) gives the right order.
**Output** is roast's MAF: header ``##maf version=1 scoring=roast.v3.3``, blocks with the reference on top, and a final ``##eof maf``. Gap annotation (``mafAddIRows``) is a separate, per-sequence step.
.. _multiz: https://github.com/multiz/multiz
